 Seamlessly manage Daikin's heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems with advanced technology designed for precise temperature control, enhanced energy efficiency, and modern convenience.

## Indoor Air Quality

 Designed with Innovation and Technology

## Perfecting The Air We Share

##### Indoor Air Quality Solutions

 Daikin's indoor air quality products help deliver enhanced indoor comfort for every season.

###### Daikin One Premium Air Cleaner

 The Daikin One Premium Air Cleaner is an in-line air cleaner that treats indoor air for certain airborne particulate matter and chemicals found in the home.

 Explore Daikin's Indoor Air Quality content, tools, and resources.

## Cloud Services & Apps

 Designed with comfort convenience in mind.

## Explore the Daikin Cloud

##### Comfort, Convenience, and Peace of Mind

 Enable Daikin One Cloud Service to create a digital connection between your HVAC system and your servicing contractor to enable a view of system needs, performance insights.

###### Daikin One Home Mobile App

 See how the Daikin One Home App lets you effortlessly manage your home's comfort, adjust settings remotely, and receive system alerts from your smartphone.

### Make your home Smarter

 Elevate your comfort and efficiency with Daikin's Smart Technology. Designed for modern lifestyles, these intelligent systems put you in complete control of your home's climate, no matter where you are.

## Experience Smart Comfort with SkyportCare

### The Daikin Ecosystem

 Daikin’s comprehensive approach to Home Comfort means a complete support system for your heating, cooling, and ventilation needs. 

Daikin One+ Smart Thermostat

The first smart thermostat to offer full two-way communications with nearly all Daikin ducted and ductless HVAC systems. 

This cloud-connected, smart thermostat measures temperature, humidity, and air quality (when connected to the Daikin One Home Air Monitor) inside your home.

Indoor AIr Quality (IAQ) Solutions

 Daikin's IAQ technologies, such as the Daikin One Home Air Monitor, Daikin One Powered Ventilator, and Daikin One Premium Air Cleaner, help improve indoor air quality using sensors in the duct system to detect airborne particles and chemicals. 

Adaptive Inverter Technology

An inverter is an energy-saving technology that helps eliminate wasted operation in air conditioners and heat pumps by efficiently controlling motor speed.

In adaptive inverter-type air conditioners and heat pumps, the temperature is adjusted by changing the motor speed without turning the motor ON and OFF. Compared to non-inverter type air conditioners, air conditioners with inverters have less power loss and can save up to 30% more energy.

# Daikin FY2026 Q2 Earnings Briefing

- Stock: 6367.T
- Call ID: JP_6367.T_2026-11-05
- Date: 2026-11-05
- Type: Earnings call

## Spokespersons

- 髙橋 (Operator)

## Summary

Daikin Industries reported its second-quarter (interim) results for the fiscal year ending March 2027 on November 5, 2026, with revenue up 17.4% year-on-year to ¥2,910.7 billion and operating profit up 9.8% to ¥270.7 billion, marking a record high for the first half. Ordinary profit rose 2.2% to ¥247.1 billion, and interim net profit attributable to owners of the parent increased 7.5% to ¥172.9 billion. Despite cost pressures exceeding initial assumptions—including heightened Middle East tensions, additional US tariffs, soaring raw material prices, and emerging-market currency weakness—the company secured profit growth by expanding sales of high-value-added products, implementing pricing measures, and pursuing total cost reduction, while also capturing the benefits of a weaker yen and US tariff refunds. However, the operating margin fell 0.6 points from 9.9% a year earlier to 9.3%, also falling short of plan.

By segment, the air conditioning and refrigeration business posted revenue of ¥2,699.6 billion, up 17.0% year-on-year, and operating profit of ¥244.3 billion, up 5.2%, achieving revenue and profit growth, but its operating margin declined 1.0 point from 10.1% to 9.1%. By region, Japan (revenue at 118% of the prior year) and Europe (121%) improved profitability through expanded sales of high-value-added products, while the Americas saw its operating margin decline due to tariffs and rising market prices. Asia also saw profitability deteriorate amid higher costs and intensifying competition. The chemical business posted strong sales of high-performance resins for semiconductors and data centers, with revenue up 25.2% to ¥158.7 billion and operating profit up 77.3% to ¥24.2 billion, a substantial profit increase, while its operating margin improved 4.4 points from 10.8% to 15.2%.

The full-year plan was revised upward, with revenue raised from the previous forecast of ¥5,150.0 billion to ¥5,440.0 billion (up 8.5% year-on-year) and operating profit from ¥436.0 billion to ¥455.0 billion (up 9.6%). The company aims to achieve record-high results. The second-half operating margin is expected to improve 0.7 points year-on-year, securing a full-year margin of 8.4%, on par with the prior year. The assumed exchange rates from the third quarter onward are ¥150 per dollar and ¥175 per euro. The annual dividend was raised by ¥10 from the previous forecast to ¥370 per share (interim ¥185, year-end ¥185).

President Naofumi Takenaka identified "re-strengthening earning power" as the top priority, emphasizing five points: transformation into a solution provider, improving profitability of the North American air conditioning business, cost structure reform, efficiency of invested capital, and turnaround of low-profit businesses. Regarding low-profit businesses in particular, he acknowledged that "the speed is insufficient relative to investor expectations" and indicated a policy of reaching early conclusions, including business withdrawal or sale. In North America, data center demand is strong, and revenue from the acquired Alliance Air is also growing. Meanwhile, in China, residential multi-split sales fell to 86% of the prior year amid the real estate downturn, and in Asia, the low-price offensive by Chinese manufacturers is a challenge.

## Operations

### Company-wide results (first half of fiscal 2026)

- Revenue: ¥2,910.7 billion (up 17.4% year-on-year; up 9% excluding FX)
- Operating profit: ¥270.7 billion (up 9.8%; up 7% excluding FX), operating margin 9.3% (down 0.6 points from 9.9% a year earlier)
- Ordinary profit: ¥247.1 billion (up 2.2%)
- Interim net profit attributable to owners of the parent: ¥172.9 billion (up 7.5%)
- FX impact: Revenue +¥200.5 billion, operating profit +¥6.0 billion (dollar-yen 159, euro-yen 184)

### By segment

- Air conditioning and refrigeration business: Revenue ¥2,699.6 billion (up 17.0%), operating profit ¥244.3 billion (up 5.2%), operating margin 9.1% (down 1.0 point from 10.1% a year earlier). Expanded sales of high-value-added products in Japan and Europe contributed, but higher costs and intensifying competition in the Americas and Asia weighed on results.
- Chemical business: Revenue ¥158.7 billion (up 25.2%), operating profit ¥24.2 billion (up 77.3%), operating margin 15.2% (up 4.4 points from 10.8%). High-performance resins for semiconductors and data centers and high-speed communications coating materials performed well.
- Other businesses: Revenue ¥52.3 billion (up 15.8%), operating profit ¥2.2 billion (up 251.3%).

### By region (air conditioning and refrigeration business)

- Japan: Revenue at 118% of the prior year. Residential demand expanded on last-minute demand ahead of energy-saving regulations and subsidies, while commercial demand for heat countermeasures remained firm.
- Americas: Revenue at 117%. DNA (residential) at 114% with a 25% share (up 2 points year-on-year). DAA (applied) at 123%, with data center demand growing significantly.
- China: Revenue at 105%. Residential multi-split fell to 86%, but commercial and applied products compensated, keeping the operating margin at a high level.
- Europe: Revenue at 121%. Significant revenue growth on heatwave demand and a recovery in heat pump heating.
- Asia and Oceania: Asia at 123% (India at 139%), Oceania at 126%. However, profitability declined due to higher costs and currency weakness.

### Financial position and cash flow

- Total assets: ¥5,841.5 billion (up ¥32.2 billion from the end of the prior fiscal year)
- Equity ratio: 51.0% (down from 55.9% at the end of the prior fiscal year)
- Interest-bearing debt ratio: 22.8% (up from 18.8% at the end of the prior fiscal year)
- Operating cash flow: ¥341.0 billion inflow (up ¥97.6 billion year-on-year)
- Share buyback: ¥350.0 billion executed (May 2026)

### Factors behind operating profit change (year-on-year)

- FX +¥6.0 billion, raw materials -¥77.0 billion (including direct US tariff impact of -¥10.3 billion and refunds of +¥12.6 billion), fixed costs and others -¥35.0 billion, sales expansion +¥49.2 billion, pricing measures +¥46.0 billion, cost reduction +¥35.0 billion.

## Outlook

### Full-year earnings forecast (fiscal year ending March 2027, revised)

- Revenue: ¥5,440.0 billion (up 8.5% year-on-year; revised up 5.6% from the previous forecast of ¥5,150.0 billion)
- Operating profit: ¥455.0 billion (up 9.6%; revised up 4.4% from the previous forecast of ¥436.0 billion), operating margin 8.4% (up 0.1 point from 8.3% a year earlier)
- Ordinary profit: ¥417.0 billion (up 2.2%)
- Net profit attributable to owners of the parent: ¥280.0 billion (up 1.7%)
- Net profit per share: ¥1,006.45
- Assumed exchange rates: From the third quarter onward, ¥150 per dollar and ¥175 per euro

### Full-year plan by segment

- Air conditioning and refrigeration business: Revenue ¥5,003.0 billion (up 8% year-on-year), operating profit ¥404.0 billion (up 7%), operating margin 8.1%. In North America, the company will expand sales and share of residential unitary products, strengthen Fit's sales capabilities, and expand data center solutions.
- Chemical business: Revenue ¥320.0 billion (up 14%), operating profit ¥45.0 billion (up 36%), operating margin 14.1%. Expand sales for semiconductors and data centers.

### Key initiatives for the second half

- Reap the benefits of pricing measures and cost reductions implemented in the first half during the second half, improving the operating margin by 0.7 points year-on-year.
- Improve the operating margin of the North American air conditioning business by 1 point for the full year (from 11% in the first half to the full-year target). Absorb cost increases through expanding Fit dealers and increasing sales per store, pricing measures, and total cost reduction.
- For data centers, three-quarters of the order backlog is already under construction, and the business impact in fiscal 2027 is expected to be limited. For the order backlog from fiscal 2028 onward, the company will begin evaluating each project individually.
- For low-profit businesses (a dozen or so businesses including the filter business and the European low-temperature business), the company will reach early conclusions, including withdrawal or sale.
- Share buybacks will not be capped at ¥700.0 billion; the company will act flexibly, prioritizing growth investments while also considering asset sales and leverage.
- The annual dividend is ¥370 per share (interim ¥185, year-end ¥185), raised by ¥10 from the previous forecast.

## Q&A Highlights

Q: What is the top-line outlook and competitive environment for Japan, Europe, and Asia?
A: In Japan, demand swelled on last-minute demand ahead of energy-saving regulations and the expansion of Tokyo Metropolitan Government subsidies, and we secured supply and fully captured the benefits. Assuming a backlash next year, we are already strengthening commercial products and addressing routes and regions where room air conditioner share is low. In Europe, we captured heatwave demand through our local production system, contributing to profit mainly in the mid-to-high-end segment. Chinese manufacturers are mounting a low-price offensive, but we differentiate ourselves in the mid-to-high-end segment. In Asia, the top line grew on recovering demand in India, but profitability declined due to Chinese manufacturers' low-price offensive, higher costs, and currency weakness. Toward next fiscal year, we will advance a three-tier strategy (premium, mid-range, and mass-market) and strengthen commercial and applied products.

Q: What is the balance between price pass-through and share for US DNA?
A: The housing market is tough due to high mortgage rates, but our policy of prioritizing profitability will not waver. We will increase the mix of high-value-added products such as Fit and strengthen light commercial and parts/solutions. Leveraging our strongest-in-North-America product lineup including R32-compatible products and VRV, we will also advance AI-driven labor savings and optimization of our branch network to ensure we raise the margin. We will maintain share while focusing on price and mix.

Q: What is driving the sales expansion effect as a profit contributor?
A: Expanded sales of high-value-added products and solutions in Europe, Asia, and Japan contributed. In North America, the consumption environment is weak and demand is shifting to cheaper products, limiting mix improvement. In the second half, factory utilization will rise on higher volumes, while production will decrease due to inventory efficiency efforts.

Q: What are the risks to data center demand and the impact of environmental policy?
A: There may be policy changes after the midterm elections, but the impact this fiscal year is limited with only five months remaining. In fiscal 2027 as well, three-quarters of the order backlog is under construction, so the impact is limited. For fiscal 2028, we will begin evaluating each project individually. The Mexico plant will have a flexible line configuration resilient to demand fluctuations, and the new plant will be established on a lease basis with investment decisions made in stages. On the environmental front, we recognize that rising electricity prices and power shortages will be tailwinds for energy-saving, high-efficiency products.

Q: How did you offset the first-half cost increases? What are the upside factors for the full-year plan?
A: In the first half, we implemented additional cost improvements in response to cost increases exceeding assumptions. We also reduced fixed costs company-wide compared with the original plan. For the full year, the structure is to cover what pricing measures cannot fully offset through cost reduction and fixed-cost efficiency. The long-term fixed-cost reduction themes of FUSION30 will bear fruit in the latter half, but the current positive results are largely due to the accumulated efforts of each department.

Q: What is the background behind the ¥90.0 billion sales expansion effect?
A: We are not pursuing volume expansion that ignores profitability, but in the past there were unprofitable products. Under FUSION30, we do not assume significant demand growth and are promoting efforts to increase the weight of high-value-added products in all regions. Since price revisions involve large cost increases, we respond by moving up new product launches, among other measures. To counter Chinese manufacturers' entry into the volume zone, we will strengthen product and sales capabilities and cost competitiveness.

Q: What is the breakdown and profitability of the 28% solution business ratio?
A: The ratio is to global air conditioning business revenue. The composition ratio of residential to commercial is 1:3 to 1:3.5. Commercial solutions grew more than 10% in the first half, but residential declined year-on-year due to lower residential multi-split sales in China. The profit margin of commercial solutions is not significantly different from that of equipment, but maintenance and parts have high gross margins, and we will improve profitability through scale expansion. Quantitative targets are not disclosed at this time.

Q: What are India's profit margin and competitive environment?
A: India's profit margin was about 8% last fiscal year, lower than other regions, and we aim to raise it to 10% or more during the FUSION30 period. Currently, rupee weakness is increasing procurement costs and slightly worsening profitability, but this is not a structural factor. We are promoting dealer development not only at the first tier but also at the second tier, leveraging the superiority of our product lineup. The challenge is the high proportion of residential products, so we will increase the commercial ratio. Our biggest rival is local manufacturers, and Chinese manufacturers are entering through OEM. We will increase the mix of system products and commercial products for affluent customers.

Q: What are the future risks of raw material costs?
A: Copper, initially assumed at $12,000 per ton, has risen to around $13,500, and we have incorporated a negative factor of over ¥10.0 billion. Parts, mainly resins, are also affected by inflation more than copper, and we expect cost increases of over ¥20.0 billion. For this fiscal year, about 70% of both copper and aluminum is hedged, but hedging for next fiscal year is not progressing, and we will prepare the budget assuming raw material prices continue to rise next fiscal year. We will accelerate substitution from copper to other materials.

Q: What is the certainty of achieving the second-half profit increase and what is the story on the ground?
A: Fit is completely different from conventional US products, so it took time, but we continue to provide detailed support globally, including installation support for the first 10 units, standing fully behind dealers. We are moving up the development and launch of differentiated products and following up monthly with individual action plans that achieve price, volume, and mix simultaneously. The field understands our system of taking additional measures in response to environmental changes.

Q: What is your thinking on next fiscal year's operating margin?
A: Copper prices are not sufficiently hedged for next fiscal year, so we are prepared for some cost increases. Fit sales expansion has been growing since the second quarter and we have high expectations for next year. Commercial solutions are also expected to improve profit as maintenance and other services grow with expansion. For next fiscal year, we are working with each business line to concretize profit growth without expecting significant revenue growth. In DNA, low-SEER products are increasing, so we will reduce costs on the growing products while firmly selling high-value-added products. For rooftop products, which are easy to install, we will launch new inverter-equipped products. We will reduce fixed costs through DX-driven labor savings and branch network optimization, positioning next fiscal year as the year to fully reap the results.

Q: Is the decline in the chemical business's second-half margin due to seasonality?
A: Production capacity is becoming quite tight, and we are considering whether we can expand sales while maintaining high efficiency. We are telling the business unit that it can do a little better in the second half.

Q: What is the competitive environment for data centers and how are acquired technologies being utilized?
A: Data center sales grew about 1.5 times from the prior year, mainly chillers. The acquired Alliance Air (custom AHUs) also grew about 40%, and the server rack cooling company grew nearly threefold. We are advancing communication with hyperscalers and strengthening packaged, modular, and containerized offerings to meet short construction and delivery needs. Competition is intense with power equipment manufacturers also entering, but we will compete through systematization leveraging our strengths.
